## My request for Codex:
OK, perform a full audit of smp.c, process.c, heap.c, libc.c, paging.c, uefi.ld, ap_trampoline.asm, cpu.c, lapic.c, and any other part of our code involved in the process, thread, and CPU.

The issue we are looking for is - even for basic commands like letters, eventually we crash the kernel, with a context guard mismatch.  This means we can isolate all the network code, all the disk code - basically anything except the above mentioned parts.

One thing to note: "Short lived" commands seem to work fine - for example, i ran "cat" on a file a hundred times, and the kernel was stable.  "letters" crashed after 10-20 seconds (depending on run)

prev_agent:
Implemented the requested repeating A–Z shell command and hooked it into the CLI.

**Changes**
- Extended the shared loop helper with a configurable delay and introduced the letters sequence plus `shell_cmd_letters`, ensuring it prints A–Z every 200 ms before wrapping (`src/sbin/cmd_loop.c:6`, `src/sbin/cmd_loop.c:10`, `src/sbin/cmd_loop.c:77`).
- Declared the new command so other modules can reference it cleanly (`include/shell_commands.h:32`).
- Advertised and registered `letters` in the shell startup banner and dispatch table so users can invoke it like other built-ins (`src/sbin/shell.c:763`, `src/sbin/shell.c:776`).

**Tests**
- `make`

**Next Steps**
- Boot the OS image and run `letters` in the shell to observe the timed output.
